transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this reinstatement review. As I understand it, we're here to discuss a student who took medical leave and has applied for reinstatement for the upcoming academic year. I've seen a draft plan that lists 12 credits for the fall term, places STAT-210 in a regular daytime section, and currently contains no disability-accommodation or financial-aid conditions. Before I make my binding decision on this plan, I'd like to hear from each of you. Our standard process calls for a cross-office review, and I want to make sure we've covered all relevant perspectives. Please share any concerns, conditions, or information your offices believe should be reflected in the final written plan the student will receive.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical discrepancy. In my advising meeting with the student this week, I confirmed that the student's continuing employment schedule permits a maximum of exactly 9 credits in the fall term. I recorded this in my advising notes. However, the reinstatement draft plan still shows 12 credits for the fall, which exceeds what the student can realistically manage given their work obligations. This needs to be corrected before the plan is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical scheduling issue with STAT-210. I checked the registrar's course inventory and confirmed that the student's required STAT-210 section is offered only online in the summer term — it is not available as a regular daytime section in the fall. The current draft plan incorrectly places STAT-210 in a fall daytime section. The plan must be corrected to move STAT-210 out of the fall daytime schedule and identify the online summer section instead. I should note that this inventory update has not yet reached the reinstatement file, which is likely why the draft still shows the fall daytime placement.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical omission in the draft plan. My completed disability-services review confirms that this student has an active accommodation requiring 1.5-times testing time and a reduced-distraction testing setting. This accommodation record has not yet been attached to the reinstatement draft, which is why the plan currently shows no disability-accommodation conditions. The final written plan must include this accommodation so the student receives a complete and accurate plan.
